summary: Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as professor at Hamburg and teaching at Copenhagen, McGill, and Renmin.

Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She has served as a faculty member at the University of Virginia and was attested in 2009 as a visiting Professor of Buddhist Art at The University of Hong Kong.

Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Yale, Banaras Hindu University, and Vanderbilt, he taught at Southern Illinois and Central Connecticut State before a long career at the University of Maine from 1974 to 2020.

Douglas Fairchild Ober specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

Douglas Gildow specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University (attested 2016), studying under supervisors Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.

Douglas Osto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Washington and a PhD from SOAS under Ulrich Pagel, later becoming Senior Lecturer and Programme Coordinator at Massey University.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins, and served as Assistant Professor at East Tennessee State University (~2008–2014).
Dragana Majhen specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's degree at the University of Manitoba under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, held posts at Marburg (attested 2002, 2020), and worked for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Dramdul works in Tibetology and Indology. He served as Director at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2007) and editor-in-chief for Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin was a Buddhist figure who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who completed an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jampal Dewé Nyima, Min Ling Orgyen Namdrol Gyatso, and Pé Kö Lama Könchok Rabten, teaching numerous prominent students.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) was a master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and other teachers, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught many disciples including Matthew T. Kapstein and Alexander Berzin.

Duncan Ryūken Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and has held posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
